questions.question: What does MCP stand for?
questions.explanation: MCP stands for Model Context Protocol — an open standard that defines how AI agents discover and call external capabilities (Tools, Resources, and Prompts) in a framework-agnostic way.

questions.question: What are the THREE universal building blocks defined by MCP?
questions.explanation: MCP defines three universal building blocks: Tools (callable functions), Resources (readable data sources), and Prompts (reusable message templates). Any MCP-compatible agent can use any MCP server's Tools, Resources, and Prompts.

questions.question: In the Agent Factory Architecture, which layer does MCP occupy?
questions.explanation: MCP occupies Layer 4 (MCP Server) in the 8-layer Agent Factory Architecture. It sits between the Claude Agent SDK (L5) and the FastAPI backend (L3), routing agent tool calls to the appropriate backend endpoints.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between an MCP Tool and an MCP Resource?

options.A: Tools are faster; Resources are slower
options.B: Tools are actions the agent calls; Resources are data sources the agent reads
options.C: Tools are for Claude; Resources are for GPT-4
options.D: Tools require authentication; Resources are public

questions.explanation: An MCP Tool is a callable action (e.g. submit_quiz, search_content). An MCP Resource is a data source the agent reads (e.g. a chapter summary at URI 'course://chapters/chapter-01/summary'). The distinction matters for how agents discover and use them.

questions.question: What are the THREE properties of a well-designed Agent Skill?
questions.explanation: A well-designed Agent Skill has: (1) Single Responsibility — does one thing only; (2) Clear Termination — has a defined endpoint so it doesn't loop; (3) API-Grounded — always fetches data from the backend API, never from the LLM's training memory.
